rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act rent cap
rules.requirement: Owners may not raise rent more than 5% plus the local CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period, and no more than twice in that period. New tenancies may start at any rent. Units under stricter local rent control are exempt.
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower
rules.effective_date_note: Current version operative 2024-04-01 (SB 567, effective 2024-01-01); the original cap applied to increases on or after 2019-03-15 per subd. (h).
rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted affordable housing; dormitories; housing under stricter local rent control; certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years; separately alienable property (e.g. single-family homes, condos) not owned by REIT/corporation/corporate-member LLC with notice; owner-occupied duplex; mobilehome owners.
rules.penalty: Civil action for injunctive relief, damages for the overcharge (up to 3x if willful), attorney's fees; AG, city attorney or county counsel may enforce.
rules.interaction: Yields to local rent control that restricts annual increases to less than the state cap; does not expand or limit local authority under Civ. Code ch. 2.7.

unverifiable_exemptions: single-family homes and condos not owned by REIT, corporation or corporate-member LLC

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act – just cause eviction and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: After a tenant has lived in a unit for 12 months, the owner can end the tenancy only for a stated at-fault or no-fault just cause. For no-fault reasons the owner must pay one month's rent in relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent, and the notice must say so.
rules.key_value: Just cause after 12 months; no-fault relocation = 1 month's rent
rules.quoted_span: after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy
rules.effective_date_note: Section operative 2024-04-01 per subd. (m); version amended by AB 1529 effective 2026-01-01. Original TPA effective 2020-01-01 (not stated in the document).
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels; nonprofit hospital/religious/care facilities; dormitories; owner shares bathroom/kitchen; owner-occupied single-family and duplex; certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years; separately alienable property owned by non-REIT/corporation with notice; deed-restricted affordable housing.
rules.penalty: Noncompliant notice is void; owner liable for actual damages, attorney's fees, up to 3x if willful; AG, city attorney or county counsel may seek injunctive relief.
rules.interaction: Does not apply where a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before 9/1/2019, or a later more protective one, applies; property cannot be subject to both.

unverifiable_exemptions: single-family homes/condos alienable separately owned by non-corporate owner with notice
dormitories, hospitals, care facilities, transient hotels

rules.title: California security deposit cap and return rules (AB 12)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not demand or receive security over one month's rent (two months for qualifying small landlords with no more than two properties and four units, except for service members), in addition to first month's rent. The deposit must be returned with an itemized statement within 21 days after the tenant vacates.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords)
rules.quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy
rules.effective_date_note: Subd. (c)(6) applies the cap to security collected on or after 2024-07-01 (AB 12); current text amended by AB 414 effective 2026-01-01.
rules.penalty: Bad faith retention may result in statutory damages up to twice the deposit plus actual damages.
rules.exemptions: Two-month cap for natural-person/natural-person-LLC landlords owning no more than two rental properties with four units total; not available for service member tenants.

coverage.landlord_size_condition: owner of 2 or fewer rental properties with no more than 4 units total (for the 2-month cap)
unverifiable_exemptions: small landlord status for two-month cap

rules.title: California application screening fee limits
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge a screening fee only up to actual out-of-pocket costs and never above $30 per applicant (CPI-adjusted annually since 1998). No fee if no unit is available; landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund unused amounts, provide the credit report, and offer first-come screening or refund to unselected applicants.
rules.key_value: $30 per applicant base, CPI-adjusted since 1998 (Berkeley page lists $68.96 for 2026)
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant
rules.effective_date_note: Effective date of the AB 1170 amendment; the cap dates from earlier versions not stated in the documents.
rules.conflict_note: The statute states a $30 base adjusted by CPI and no current figure; the Berkeley Rent Board page (D005) states $68.96 as the 2026 maximum. No single official statewide 2026 figure is confirmed.

rules.title: FEHA housing discrimination: source of income protections
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate against or harass applicants or tenants based on source of income, including Section 8 and HUD-VASH vouchers. For subsidized tenants, income standards must be based on the tenant's share of rent and applicants may offer alternative evidence instead of credit history. Landlords may still ask about the level or source of income.
rules.key_value: ban on source-of-income discrimination incl. Section 8 and HUD-VASH vouchers
rules.quoted_span: For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person.
rules.effective_date_note: SB 267 amendment effective 2024-01-01 (HUD-VASH, credit-history provisions); SB 329 added subsidies to source of income effective 2020-01-01 per D015.
rules.exemptions: Owner occupying a home and renting to one additional person; shared living area; senior housing.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied home renting to one additional person

rules.title: California Civil Rights Council criminal history regulations (housing)
rules.requirement: Landlords may check criminal history but may not use blanket bans on people with a criminal history, consider arrests without conviction, sealed/expunged or juvenile records, and may deny based on a conviction only if directly related to being a good tenant or safety.
rules.key_value: no blanket criminal-history bans; no arrests without conviction
rules.citation: California Civil Rights Council criminal history regulations (FEHA)
citation_aliases: Civil Rights Council criminal history regulations
rules.quoted_span: Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
rules.effective_date_note: Regulations took effect 2020-01-01 per D015 (secondary). Specific regulation section not stated in the documents.
rules.review_note: Regulation section not stated in the documents, so cited by name.

rules.title: AB 325 / SB 763 – Common pricing algorithm prohibition (Cartwright Act)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software using competitor data to influence prices) as part of a conspiracy to restrain trade, or to use or distribute one while coercing others to adopt its recommended prices. Higher criminal and civil penalties apply.
rules.key_value: ban on common pricing algorithms using competitor data in restraint of trade or with coercion
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter
rules.effective_date_note: AB 325 chaptered 2025-10-06; 2026-01-01 effective date stated in D028 (law-firm alert).
rules.penalty: Criminal fines up to $6 million (corporations) or $1 million (individuals), civil fines up to $1 million in AG/DA actions, treble damages in private suits (per D028).
rules.exemptions: End consumers; single-firm algorithms using only own data are not covered.

Screening-fee dollar figure disagrees across sources ($30 base vs $68.96 for 2026 on Berkeley page).
